title: spec review: S2h external skill hardening: structured risk report at inspection (scripts, endpoints, tools, credential references, dependencies, filesystem) gating quarantined to testing (P21)
spec:
orchestrator/skill_discovery.inspect(): extend the report with risk = {scripts: [{path, shebang or extension, executable bit}], endpoints: [hosts and URLs found in any file], tools: [names from the skill frontmatter allowed-tools or tools fields and Bash/shell mentions], credential_refs: [environment variable names matching KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSWD|CREDENTIAL|AUTH and mentions of dotenv or credential files, names only], dependencies: [packages from requirements, pyproject, package.json, pip or npm install lines], filesystem: [absolute paths, home-directory references, recursive delete or chmod commands], scan: the context_scanner verdict per file from S1d, level: low|medium|high with reasons}. Level rules: high when scan is blocked anywhere, or an endpoint plus a credential_ref both appear, or a recursive delete or permission change appears, or a dependency is installed from a URL or git source; medium when any script, endpoint, dependency or credential_ref exists; low otherwise. Persist the report next to the quarantine content as inspection.json (reserved name check like the existing quarantine report filename rule). orchestrator/skills_registry.transition(): a quarantined skill may move to testing only when its latest inspection report exists, its content hash matches, and level is not high and scan is not blocked; otherwise raise ValueError naming the reasons unless the transition reason starts with 'human-reviewed:' (record that in the state document). CLI: `orchestrator skills inspect <id>` prints the risk report; `skills list` shows the level. Docs: docs/hermes-hardening/14-skill-hardening.md.
Repository rules: unittest (not pytest), tests/_harness.py single ORCH_ROOT fixture; every acceptance test id tests/test_<module>.py::test_name is a method def test_name(self) in a unittest.TestCase. No new third-party dependencies. Never write secret values to any file or log; test fixtures use synthetic names and values that are not credential-shaped. Do not quote template placeholder tokens (double braces) anywhere in code comments or docs. Shadow-first: a new adaptive path never changes what a worker sees until its mode is active; shadow only writes decision_log or runs rows. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh . until green; the base suite must stay green. Do not ask questions: decide, and note decisions in the result summary. The interface contracts of the stage 1 modules are in .orchestrator/plan.md (section GOAL T-0991) and in docs/hermes-hardening/0*.md on this branch; read the merged module before building on it.
acceptance: tests/test_skill_discovery.py::test_risk_report_levels_from_fixture_skills (a benign skill low, a script-plus-endpoint skill medium, an endpoint-plus-credential skill high, a blocked-scan skill high)

risks.issue: Spec adds a reserved-name check for inspection.json in _bounded() but the three sites that hash quarantine directory contents to validate record["content_hash"] (inspect()'s own file listing ~line 285, check_upstream()'s old-dir listing ~line 346, and skills_registry._testing_findings() ~line 360) only exclude "findings.json" by name. If inspect() also writes inspection.json into the same directory, every subsequent inspect()/check_upstream()/transition() call will hash the new file in and falsely report "quarantine content changed".

_testing_findings() (line 346) today blocks quarantined->testing on any block-severity finding or the mere presence of a script, requiring an "override:" reason (see tests/test_skill_discovery.py:157-166, 269-279). The spec's new level rule only blocks when level==high, so a skill with just a script, one credential_ref, or one endpoint (all "medium" under the spec's own rules) would no longer be blocked at all -- silently weakening an already-shipped control. The spec doesn't say whether the new gate replaces, wraps, or coexists with the old one, and the one acceptance test named only covers the new high-risk path.

rollback() (line 395) also re-enters "testing" via the same _testing_findings() call (line 407-408), and tests/test_skill_discovery.py:211-220 exercises that path. The spec only names transition(), leaving rollback() on the old gate and creating an inconsistent bar for re-entering testing depending on which code path is used.

Existing tests hard-assert the inspection report is persisted as findings.json with exact content equality (lines 155, 180, 194, 206, 216, 219). The spec says to "extend the report" (implying findings.json is extended) but then says to persist it "as inspection.json", without saying whether inspection.json replaces findings.json (breaking these filename assertions) or is written alongside it (duplicating the report under two names with no reconciliation stated).

suggested_spec_changes: State explicitly whether inspect() renames its report file from findings.json to inspection.json, and if so, update the existing findings.json-based assertions in tests/test_skill_discovery.py as part of this task's scope.

Add inspection.json (or the chosen filename) to every content-hash exclusion site: skill_discovery.inspect()'s file listing, skill_discovery.check_upstream()'s old-dir listing, and skills_registry._testing_findings()'s file listing -- not just the _bounded() reserved-name check.

Specify precisely how the new level-based gate relates to the existing block-severity/script gate in _testing_findings: either state that level replaces the old severity/script check entirely (and add acceptance coverage proving scripts/credentials/destructive findings still block without human review), or state both gates must pass and define how 'override:' and 'human-reviewed:' reasons compose.

Extend the transition() gate change to rollback(), or explicitly state rollback() keeps the old gate and why that's acceptable, given rollback() shares _testing_findings() and existing tests cover that path.
